hero_tagline: Symbols that actually survive PUBG Mobile and BGMI's own in-game font, not just another generic Unicode dump. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: PUBG Mobile and BGMI (Battlegrounds Mobile India: same game, India release) don't render text with your phone's full system font. They ship a small bundled font that covers only a few thousand of Unicode's 150,000+ characters, which is why a symbol that looks fine everywhere else can show up as a blank square, or get flatly rejected, in your in-game name. Every character on this page is a single-character pick from the families players actually report working: katakana and CJK marks, Javanese frame brackets, and simple stars. Names are capped at 14 characters total, so a frame counts against your limit before you've typed a single letter. Copy what you need and build around it.

PUBG Mobile and BGMI don't use your phone's system font to render display names: they use a font bundled inside the game client, which covers only a fraction of Unicode's 150,000+ characters. A symbol can be completely valid Unicode and still fail here, not because it's "banned," but because the game's own font simply has no glyph drawn for it: it shows up as a blank box, or the game rejects the whole name outright. This is a different failure mode than a content filter, and it's why a symbol that works perfectly on Instagram or Discord can break specifically in PUBG. Single-character picks from the Battle-Tested Symbols section above are chosen because they're inside that smaller, actually-supported set. Multi-symbol combos and rarer Unicode blocks carry more risk.

faq.q: Which symbols actually work in PUBG Mobile / BGMI names?
faq.a: Single-character CJK, katakana, and common decorative marks (ツ, 彡, 乂, 亗, 々, ム, ★, ✦) are the most reliable, because PUBG Mobile and BGMI render text using a limited in-app font, not your device's full system font. Every symbol in the Battle-Tested Symbols section above is chosen from that reliably-rendering set.

faq.q: What's the difference between PUBG Mobile and BGMI names?
faq.a: BGMI (Battlegrounds Mobile India) is Krafton's India-market release of PUBG Mobile: same engine, same client font, same name-field behavior. A symbol that works in one works in the other. The names differ by region/publisher, not by rendering rules, so this page serves both without a separate list.

faq.q: Why does PUBG show "invalid characters" for a symbol that works elsewhere?
faq.a: PUBG Mobile and BGMI bundle their own client font, which covers only a few thousand of Unicode's 150,000+ characters: a symbol can be perfectly valid Unicode and still render as a blank box or get rejected outright if it's outside that set. This is different from an emoji or a font-styling problem; it's specific to which glyphs the game's own font ships with. If a symbol fails, try a simpler single-character pick from the Battle-Tested section above before assuming your name is the problem.

faq.q: How many characters can a PUBG Mobile or BGMI name have?
faq.a: 14 characters, including any symbols. A frame like ꧁ ꧂ already uses 2 of those 14 before you type a single letter, so heavier decoration eats into how much of your actual name fits. Count your symbols, not just your letters.

faq.q: Can I preview a name before spending a rename card?
faq.a: The game itself will reject invalid characters at the confirmation screen before it charges a rename card, so nothing here can get spent on a name that outright fails. What it won't warn you about is a symbol that saves but renders as a blank square for other players on a different device: that's a display-side risk, not a validation error, which is exactly why this page sticks to the smaller set of symbols with the most consistent real-world reports of working.

faq.q: Do PUBG name symbols work the same on Android and iOS?
faq.a: Mostly, since both platforms use the game's own bundled font rather than the device's system font, but player reports of edge-case differences (a rarer symbol rendering on one OS and not the other) show up often enough that it's worth treating as a real possibility, not a myth. Single-character picks from the Battle-Tested section are the safest bet across both.
